one_liner: Goes in the too-hard pile: its industry is changing too fast to predict and the business is too complex or uncertain to forecast. No verdict on price.

profile.what: Tesla makes electric cars (Model 3, Model Y, Cybertruck), battery storage for homes and power grids, and solar products. It is also developing self-driving software, a robotaxi service and humanoid robots.
profile.money: About 70% of 2025 revenue came from selling cars. Energy storage (Megapack, Powerwall) is about 14% and growing quickly. Services, charging and regulatory credits sold to other carmakers make up the rest. Car profit margins have fallen as Tesla cut prices to defend volume.
profile.valued: Tesla is not valued on today's car business: its P/E is far above any carmaker's. The price rests on expectations for robotaxis, self-driving software and robots, so it moves with sentiment about those projects rather than with car deliveries.

summary.sentence: An electric-car maker valued almost entirely on robotaxis and robots that are not yet businesses.
strengths: Net cash and a large energy-storage business.
Autonomy would transform the economics if it works.
risks: Net income has fallen about 80% from its 2023 level.
Returns on capital are now below 5%.

financial_health.ratio_gaps: Not available from the data source, so not shown: a ten-year record, inventory and receivables turnover, the quick ratio, goodwill and tangible book value, and maintenance capex split from growth capex. Owner earnings therefore deduct all capex, which is conservative.

valuation.method: Fair value is the average of two methods: (1) Owner cash flow, capex held at depreciation: $7.2B a year: operating cash flow less depreciation and stock-based pay (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM). Capex is running at 2.3x depreciation, so most of it is expansion, not upkeep. (2) Damodaran: cash flow to the firm: Sales grow 12–18% for five years, fading to 3%; operating margin held at 3%; cost of capital 10.7%. Cash added, debt subtracted. The owner cash flow method grows the cash for five years, then at half that rate, 3% after year ten, discounted at 10%. Stock-based pay is deducted because it is a real cost to owners.
